Let’s dive into Chapter 5: Building a Repeatable System—Tools and Habits for Strategic Selling.
Now, here’s where everything comes together. Up to this point, you’ve picked up strategies and ideas—maybe even tried a few. But, what if you could turn all those scattered tactics into a reliable, repeatable system? That’s what separates average salespeople from the real pros.
In complex sales, it’s not about getting lucky or having a magnetic personality. Success comes from careful planning, disciplined follow-through, and a drive to learn as you go. The best salespeople? They lean on simple, practical tools and habits to stay on track, stay focused, and stay ready for anything.
One tool you’ll want in your kit is called the “Blue Sheet.” Think of it as your sales GPS—a structured planning sheet that helps you map out every opportunity in detail. Here’s what the Blue Sheet nudges you to do:
First, jot down all the key players and what roles they play.
Then, get clear on what matters to each person—their motivations, their worries, and how much they’re rooting for you.
Next, spot any red flags. What could trip you up? And how can you tackle those issues head-on?
Finally, list out the steps you’ll need to take to keep things moving forward.
Here’s something to pay attention to—the Blue Sheet isn’t just a one-and-done. It’s a living, breathing document. As things change or new info comes in, you update it. That way, you can see where you’re missing details, anticipate bumps in the road, and make sure you’re always in sync with your client’s needs.
Beyond tools, it’s really about habits. The best salespeople make these part of their daily routine:
Preparation. Before every meeting or call, they look over the latest updates, review who’s involved, and know exactly what needs to happen next.
Analysis. After each conversation, they pause and reflect. What did they learn? What’s changed? What’s the next move?
Flexibility. When new info pops up or someone’s priorities shift, they’re ready to adjust their approach.
And finally, collaboration. They work closely with teammates, coaches—even the client—to find solutions together.
Here’s an analogy that might help: think of strategic selling as tending a garden. You can’t just plant seeds and walk away. It takes regular care, watching for changes, and adapting when the weather shifts. The goal isn’t just to “close” a deal—it’s to grow a relationship that lasts and keeps producing over time.
Want a real-world example? Imagine a sales team tracking a big account using the Blue Sheet. Midway through, they notice one key User Buyer suddenly isn’t as engaged. After updating the Blue Sheet and talking it through, they realize a recent shake-up at the company has changed that person’s priorities. So, they shift their strategy, address the new concerns, and keep the deal moving forward.
So, here’s the key takeaway. When you build a repeatable system—using tools like the Blue Sheet and habits like preparation, analysis, and flexibility—you bring order to the chaos of complex sales. Not only does it up your chances of landing the deal in front of you, but it also builds the skills and confidence you’ll need for a whole career of wins down the road.
